title: zkVC: Fast Zero-Knowledge Proof for Private and Verifiable Computing
problem: Zero-knowledge proofs (ZKP), especially zkSNARKs, remain computationally intensive for basic operations like matrix multiplication, requiring extensive constraint systems and creating significant overhead.
motivation: Cloud computing requires verifiable computation without leaking server intellectual property; zkSNARKs enable this but are too slow for practical deployment in verification-heavy workloads.
method: Zero-knowledge proofs normally work by encoding computations into vast systems of mathematical constraints, which is expensive to evaluate. zkVC cuts this overhead by introducing Constraint-reduced Polynomial Circuits (CRPC)—a technique that uses far fewer constraints—and Prefix-Sum Query (PSQ), which efficiently aggregates partial results. These optimizations specifically target matrix multiplication, the bottleneck operation in zero-knowledge proof systems.
key_novelty: zkVC uses constraint-reduced polynomial circuits to dramatically lower the constraint overhead needed to prove operations like matrix multiplication while keeping the proofs cryptographically secure.
contributions: Constraint-reduced Polynomial Circuit (CRPC) reducing matrix multiplication proof constraints
Prefix-Sum Query (PSQ) module for efficient aggregation in ZKP
12x improvement in proof generation speed over prior zkSNARK methods

metrics.speedup: 12x faster proof generation vs prior methods

limitations: Not discussed—focus on computational optimization without hardware constraint analysis.
primary_theme: Constraint-reduced zero-knowledge proofs for fast matrix verification
